children: The following are significant news stories, press reports and events on Tuesday. ALL TIMES GMT (Poland: GMT + 1 hour):

Thousands of people took part in a silent march through Krakow on Monday evening along with Poland's president and prime minister as the country tries to come to terms with an unprecedented mass shooting, in which a Polish man killed six people on the southern city's main square.

The shooting in Krakow triggered the emergence of online communities - so-called 'TCC' (True Crime Community) groups - that began to build a cult around the killer, Rzeczpospolita daily reported. Social media was also flooded with a wave of misinformation, which reached a cumulative total of over 200 million views, according to the newspaper.
Polish cities are closing their historic centres to cars and increasing the number of security patrols in response to the attack in Krakow's Main Market Square, Rzeczpospolita reported.

Senate Speaker Malgorzata Kidawa-Blonska has set the period from November 9 to November 25 (up to 12:00 PM) for senators to submit nominations for two new members of the Monetary Policy Council (MPC), state news agency PAP reported.

If there are no government measures to lower fuel prices in January and inflation significantly exceeds 4%, then the MPC may want to raise interest rates, Ludwik Kotecki, a former MPC member appointed to the central bank's management board told Parkiet daily.

Polish Defence Minister Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz left for a trip to Washington, he said on X early on Tuesday. An agreement concerning cooperation between the Polish and American defence industries could be signed during his visit, he told TVN24 on Monday evening.
